# Hermes Agent: New User FAQ & Onboarding Guide

## 1. Getting Started & Architecture

### Is there a Web UI, or is Hermes Agent CLI-only?
Hermes includes a first-party web dashboard. Run:
```bash
hermes dashboard
```
This launches a local web server at `http://127.0.0.1:9119` featuring a web interface and an embedded TUI chat tab.

### Supported Operating Systems & Environments
- **Linux & macOS:** Full native support (install via the `curl | bash` script). Multi-arch Docker images (`linux/amd64` and `linux/arm64`) run natively on Apple Silicon and Raspberry Pi.
- **Windows:** Windows 10/11 is a Tier-1 supported platform via the official PowerShell installer (`install.ps1`). *Note:* WSL2 is recommended only if you require the web dashboard's `/chat` embedded POSIX terminal pane.
- **Android (Termux):** Supported out-of-the-box via `install.sh`, using curated `termux-all` dependencies and custom temp directory routing.

### NAS Docker Deployments (Permission Errors)
If deploying via Docker on Linux NAS environments (e.g., UGOS Pro, Synology, unRAID) and encountering `[Errno 13] Permission denied` on mounted volumes (`/opt/data`), set the container environment variables:
```bash
-e PUID=1000 -e PGID=10
```
Hermes will automatically remap internal user permissions before starting services.

---

## 2. LLM Providers & Model Configuration

### Setting up Local & Custom Endpoints (Ollama, LocalAI)
When configuring local or OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints:
- **Avoid Auto-Detection Conflicts:** If you have remote keys (e.g., `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`) set in your environment, `provider: auto` might prioritize them. Explicitly set `provider: custom`:
  ```yaml
  model:
    default: ollama/your-model-name
    provider: custom
    base_url: http://localhost:11434/v1
  fallback_providers: []
  ```
- **Vision Models:** For custom/Ollama vision models, set `supports_vision: true` in your model config to preserve image payloads.
- **Ollama Cloud:** Supported natively via `provider: ollama-cloud` (routing automatically targets `https://ollama.com/v1`).

### Azure AI Foundry & Google Gemini Setup
- **Azure AI Foundry:** Run `hermes setup` to auto-detect `ANTHROPIC_FOUNDRY_BASE_URL` or configure `provider: azure-foundry`. Claude Code-specific variables (such as `CLAUDE_CODE_USE_FOUNDRY`) are not used by Hermes.
- **Google Gemini:** Use Google AI Studio API keys (`GOOGLE_API_KEY` or `GEMINI_API_KEY`). Legacy Gemini CLI OAuth flows are disabled.
- **Claude Pro/Max Subscriptions:** Anthropic requires OAuth authentication to utilize Claude Pro/Max usage tiers. Passing direct API keys will be billed under standard Anthropic API rates.

### Model Routing Policy
Hermes Agent does **not** support automatic complexity-based routing (e.g., `smart_model_routing`) or per-turn cost switching. Model selection remains tied to your configured primary model or subagent delegation (`delegation.provider` / `delegation.model`). Manual model switching is handled via `/model` or `hermes chat -m <model-name>`.

---

## 3. Messaging Gateways & Chat Platforms

Configure integrations interactively with:
```bash
hermes gateway setup
```

### Discord, Telegram, Matrix, DingTalk Features
- **Telegram & Discord Authorization:** Prevent "Unauthorized user" errors by configuring explicit allowlists or pairing:
  ```yaml
  telegram:
    allow_from: "123456789" # Authorized User ID (not chat/channel ID)
  ```
  Alternatively, approve pairing requests via `hermes pairing approve <platform> <code>`.
- **File & Attachment Support:** Hermes accepts text/code attachments (e.g., `.txt`, `.py`) and can send generated files/reports directly back across Matrix, Email (SMTP), Telegram, and Discord. DingTalk delivers image URLs using native Markdown embeds (`![image](url)`).
- **Per-Channel Personas:** Use `channel_prompts` in your config to assign distinct system prompts per channel or group across Discord, Telegram, Slack, and Mattermost.
- **Multi-Account Profiles:** Run multiple user/bot identities (e.g., Weixin, Telegram) using profiles (`hermes --profile <name>`) either as isolated processes or in a multiplexed gateway.

---

## 4. Tools, Skills, Memory, & Extensions

### Tool Limits & Long-Running Tasks
- Small local models (e.g., 4B/9B) can experience high latency due to Hermes loading its standard ~45-tool schema. Run `hermes tools` to disable unused toolsets, set `terminal.backend: local`, or switch to 32B+ models.
- The default turn limit per session is 90 (`agent.max_turns`). Override it per session with `hermes chat --max-turns <N>`.
- For persistent, multi-turn task completion without babysitting, use:
  ```text
  /goal <your task description>
  /goal resume
  ```

### Memory Architecture & Custom Extensions
- **Identity & Preferences:** Agent persona is stored in `~/.hermes/SOUL.md`. User profiles/preferences are stored in `~/.hermes/USER.md` (via `target="user"`), keeping context separate from working scratchpad memory (`MEMORY.md`).
- **Local Memory Backends:** Honcho local instances (`http://localhost:8000`) accept placeholder `"local"` API keys automatically.
- **Custom Tools & Plugins:** To add custom tools, package them as plugins under `~/.hermes/plugins/` and enable them via `hermes plugins enable <name>`. *Note:* In-tree memory provider additions are closed; memory extensions must be installed via `~/.hermes/plugins/`.
- **Observability & Analytics:** Enable Langfuse call tracing via `hermes plugins enable observability/langfuse`. Inspect skill loads and usage with `hermes insights` or `/insights`.

---

## 5. Security & Vulnerabilities
Report all security issues privately via [GitHub Security Advisories](https://github.com/NousResearch/hermes-agent/security/advisories/new) or by emailing **security@nousresearch.com**. Do not file public issues for vulnerabilities.
